confirmed.title: Double-tapping a locked card opens the lock moment and closes it again straight away (Mino's line is cut off)
confirmed.scenario: A 3-4 year old double-taps a locked menu card such as Pazar, Pasta or Dedektif, which young children do all the time. Tap 1 opens the lock moment with Mino and the swinging padlock. Tap 2 lands on the cream backdrop, because the card is centred and at most 380px wide and the tapped card is usually outside it. That closes the lock moment about 100-300 ms after it opened. The child sees a flash. Mino's 'Bunu anne-babanla açabilirsin' never plays because its 350 ms timer is cleared in bitir(). A third quick tap goes through the fading overlay (pointer-events:none on .cikiyor) and reopens it, so the overlay flickers. The same backdrop-close pattern hits the parental gate when the corner button is double-tapped (src/ui/ebeveyn-kapisi.ts:173).
confirmed.evidence: kilit-ani.ts:144 `perde.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.target === perde && bitir('kapat'));` is active from the moment the overlay is appended (line 153). There is no grace period, and the double-tap guard on line 80 only stops a second overlay from opening, not the backdrop close. The overlay is full-screen (`.kl-perde{position:fixed;inset:0;place-items:center}`, abonelik.css:509) and `.kl-kart` is `width:min(100%,380px)`. bitir() clears `zamanlar`, which holds the 350 ms konus timer (lines 126, 159).
reasons:
CONFIRM: This does happen to users of the store app, though the line numbers are wrong. kilit-ani.ts has 121 lines. The backdrop close is at line 100 (not 144), the double-tap guard is at line 36 (not 80), the append is at line 109 and the 350 ms konus timer is at lines 114-119. The code itself matches the claim.

How it gets triggered in the app (uygulama/src/ekranlar.ts:218-232): a click on a locked card calls kilitliIcerik(app.kok). That calls kilitAniAc synchronously (ekran.ts:74), which appends the full-screen .kl-perde straight away (abonelik.css:509, position:fixed, inset:0, z-index:85; the card is width:min(100%,380px)). The handler `perde.addEventListener('click', e => e.target === perde && bitir('kapat'))` is live from that moment and has no grace period. The guard at line 36 only stops a second overlay from opening.

Nothing delays or swallows the second click. The page uses touch-action:manipulation (ana.css:33), so there is no double-tap-zoom delay and every tap produces a click. A second tap that lands outside the card hits the perde and calls bitir. bitir clears the zamanlar timers (line 82), so Mino's 'selam' and the konus line never run, and sonSoyleme is not updated. A third tap passes through .cikiyor (pointer-events:none) to the menu card and reopens the overlay, because the guard skips `.cikiyor`. The same backdrop pattern is at ebeveyn-kapisi.ts:173, reached from the corner button (ekranlar.ts:248-251).

Where it can happen: the website never hits this, because kilitlerEtkin() needs both uygulamaPlatformu() and a RevenueCat key (ortam.ts:50), and nothing is locked otherwise. Release app builds get the key from CI (android.yml:50 and the revenuecat group in codemagic.yaml), so locks are on in the shipped app. The impact is a flicker and a cut-off line, not a crash, but it is reachable.

The backdrop close is at line 100 (`perde.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.target === perde && bitir('kapat'))`), the append is at 109, the double-tap guard is at 36, timers are cleared at 82, and the 350 ms konus timer is at 115.

The app sets touch-action:manipulation (ana.css:33, mino.css:5) and user-scalable=no (index.html:5). That puts it at roughly medium-low, but it is real and visible. ebeveyn-kapisi.ts:173 has the same pattern, as claimed.

confirmed.title: iOS paywall offers 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' to parents who are no longer eligible for the trial
confirmed.scenario: A parent who already used the free trial on this Apple ID (reinstall, second device, or re-subscribing after cancelling) opens the paywall. It shows '7 gün ücretsiz dene', a 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' button and 'Deneme bitince ₺X / yıl'. Apple charges them immediately. This is misleading purchase copy, which App Review flags under guideline 3.1.2, and it can lead to refund requests.
confirmed.evidence: deneme(): `if (u.introPrice && u.introPrice.price === 0) return denemeGunu(u.introPrice.periodUnit, ...)`. On iOS introPrice describes the product, not whether this user is eligible for it. Purchases.checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility is never called anywhere. ekran.ts:153-157 then sets `basla.textContent = gun ? 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' : 'Abone ol'` and builds the trial copy from that value. On Android, defaultOption.freePhase only comes from offers Play reports as eligible, so this is iOS-only.
reasons: CONFIRM: The path is reachable in the shipped iOS app. The workflow is codemagic.yaml ios-testflight, which uses the env group "revenuecat". That group supplies REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY, and vite.config.ts:65 injects it into the build. ortam.ts:40-43 then returns the key for p==='ios', and satin.ts:48 calls kur(), which loads revenueCatSaglayici (satin.ts:40, because UYGULAMA_DERLEMESI is set). From there ekran.ts yukle() calls s.planlar(), which runs deneme(u) for each package (revenuecat.ts:51). On iOS, defaultOption is null, so line 19 decides the trial purely from u.introPrice.price===0. introPrice is static product metadata (StoreKit introductoryOffer / RevenueCat introductoryDiscount). It does not depend on the user's eligibility, and no code anywhere calls checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility (grep finds nothing). planGoster (ekran.ts:153-157) then shows 'X gün ücretsiz dene', 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' and 'Deneme bitince ...' to any Apple ID that already used the trial. No guard exists. The bug cannot happen on the website: there saglayici() returns null and the paywall shows 'Yakında'. It also cannot happen in a build without the key. The iOS store build is a real shipping target, so the claim holds.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this one. The bug is real, it can happen on iOS, and nothing shows it was done on purpose. In src/abonelik/revenuecat.ts:16-21, deneme() only falls back to `introPrice.price === 0` on iOS, because defaultOption is Android-only. introPrice describes the product in StoreKit and does not depend on the user. The SDK's own docs at node_modules/@revenuecat/purchases-capacitor/dist/esm/definitions.d.ts:~475-488 say checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility is the call that decides "whether you show the user the normal product price or the introductory price". They also say to show non-intro pricing when the status is unknown, "to not create a misleading situation". A grep of src/ finds no call to it. The path is live: ios/ is committed, codemagic.yaml builds iOS for TestFlight, and planlar() feeds denemeGun straight into ekran.ts:153-157. That code sets the 'X gün ücretsiz dene' text, the 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' button and 'Deneme bitince ₺X / yıl', so a parent with no trial left still sees trial copy. Nothing in the comments, ORTAK_NOTLAR.md (the 2026-10-02/03 subscription entries say only that price and trial come from the store) or the tests shows the team knew about trial eligibility. Two things soften it. The screen is behind the parent gate, so children are not affected. Apple's own payment sheet shows the real price before the parent confirms, so the claim that they are charged without warning is overstated. The app's own copy is still misleading purchase text on a reinstall or re-subscribe, so medium severity is fair.

CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug is real. The app is built for iOS: ayar.ts:10 sets iosAnahtar and passes it to revenueCatSaglayici. In revenuecat.ts:19, deneme() shows a trial whenever the product's introPrice.price === 0. On iOS, RevenueCat's introPrice describes the product itself, not whether this user can still get the trial, and RevenueCat's docs say to call checkTrialOrIntroductoryPriceEligibility for that. The repo never calls it: a grep for 'Eligib' finds nothing. So for a parent who already used the trial or is coming back after cancelling, denemeGun is still 7. ekran.ts:153-156 then shows '7 gün ücretsiz dene', a 'Ücretsiz denemeyi başlat' button and 'Deneme bitince ...'. Nothing between those two steps checks eligibility. Android avoids this because defaultOption.freePhase only includes offers Play reports as eligible. The impact is real but limited. Apple's own purchase sheet shows the correct immediate price, so the parent is not charged without seeing it. Still, the in-app copy promises a trial they won't get. That can lead to complaints, refund requests and possible App Review issues under guideline 3.1.2. Medium severity is reasonable.

confirmed.title: Opening the album during a round, then pressing Back, restarts the round (Kartlar and Hafıza Oyunu)
confirmed.scenario: A child answers 5 of 8 questions. Each earned card flies into the big orange album button, which invites a tap. They tap it, look at the album and press Back. The game starts over from question 1 with a new set of questions, the progress dots are empty and the 5 answers count for nothing (no stars, no round counted). In Hafıza Oyunu, found pairs are lost and the board is reshuffled. Rewards earned before the detour are also not counted for 'new pack unlocked' at the end of the new round, because albumOnce is read again when the screen is rebuilt.
confirmed.evidence: In game, `albumDugmesi(() => app.git('album', { tema: tema.id }))` (src/screens/oyun.ts:74; same in src/screens/hafizaOyunu.ts:46). The album's Back button calls `app.geri()` (album.ts:140). `Uygulama.geri()` pops `{ad:'oyun', param:{tema}}` and calls `this.git(onceki.ad, onceki.param)` (src/uygulama.ts geri()), which rebuilds the screen from its factory. `oyunEkrani` then runs `turOlustur(yas, tema.id)` again with `sira = 0`, and `const albumOnce = durum.i.album.length` (oyun.ts:58-67); `hafizaOyunuEkrani` builds `new HafizaDurumu(hafizaDestesi(...))` with a fresh random deck. No round state is kept across the detour.
reasons: CONFIRM: The bug is reachable in both the app build and the website. src/oyun.ts registers 'oyun', 'hafiza' and 'album' as screens. During a round, the album button is visible and clickable: oyun.ts:75 / hafizaOyunu.ts:46 create albumDugmesi(() => app.git('album', {tema})), and it sits in the ust-cubuk at oyun.ts:88 / hafizaOyunu.ts:75. No CSS hides or disables it (no .album-dugme rule in src/styles). Pressing Back in the album calls app.geri() (album.ts:140). Uygulama.geri() pops the history entry {ad:'oyun', param} that git() pushed, sets aktifAd=null and calls git(onceki.ad, onceki.param). git() always calls the factory f(this, param) again and closes the old screen (eski.kapat(), el.remove()), with no caching or restore. So oyunEkrani runs turOlustur() again with sira=0 and empty yeniKartlar/ilerleme. hafizaOyunuEkrani builds a new HafizaDurumu with a Math.random deck. The albumOnce point also holds: cards are pushed to durum.i.album and saved immediately (oyun.ts:225-226), so the rebuilt screen's albumOnce = durum.i.album.length already includes them, and yeniAcilanlar(albumOnce, ...) in bitir() (oyun.ts:256) will not report packs unlocked by cards earned before the detour. The cards themselves stay in the album, but the round's progress, stars and turSayisi are lost.

CONFIRM: The bug is real, and nothing I found marks it as intended. In oyun.ts:74 and hafizaOyunu.ts:46 the album button calls app.git('album', {tema}). It is active for the whole round: no guard disables or hides it, and the flying cards land on it (artir/yapisEsne). In uygulama.ts, git() pushes {ad:'oyun', param} onto gecmis. The album's Back button (album.ts:140, app.geri()) pops that entry, sets aktifAd=null and calls git('oyun', param), which runs the factory again from scratch. That means turOlustur(yas, tema.id) makes a new random set of questions, sira=0, the progress dots are rebuilt empty, and albumOnce = durum.i.album.length is read again (oyun.ts:58-67). Hafıza Oyunu likewise rebuilds a fresh HafizaDurumu deck. No round state is cached anywhere. On intent: ORTAK_NOTLAR.md:22 only guarantees that cards are saved immediately ("turu yarıda bırakmak kazanılanı silmez"), so the cards themselves are not lost. But nothing says opening the album should restart the round. The sister Okul game does the opposite on purpose: "Yarıda çıkılan oda kaldığı etkinlikten sürer" (ORTAK_NOTLAR.md:339). The only e2e test (tests/e2e/akis.spec.ts:53) opens the album from the themes screen, never mid-round. Because albumOnce is re-read, a pack unlocked by cards earned before the detour is never celebrated at the end of the new round (yeniAcilanlar(albumOnce, ...), oyun.ts:256 and hafizaOyunu.ts:189). So a child loses round progress and stars, and may miss the unlock celebration, by tapping a button the game itself draws attention to. The cards are kept, so medium severity seems fair.

CONFIRM: I traced the code and the bug is real. The album button sits in the top bar during play in both games (oyun.ts:75/88, hafizaOyunu.ts:46/75). It is never disabled, and every earned card flies into it, which invites the tap. album.ts:140 calls app.geri(). geri() (uygulama.ts:110-116) pops {ad:'oyun', param:{tema}} and calls git(), and git() always runs the screen factory again: f(this, param) at line 87, with no cache or saved state. oyunEkrani then calls turOlustur() again with sira=0, fresh empty progress dots and an empty yeniKartlar. hafizaOyunuEkrani builds a new HafizaDurumu from a deck shuffled with Math.random. A child would clearly see it: the progress dots empty out, question 1 comes back with different questions (or the memory board is reshuffled), and the answers given so far earn no stars and no finished round. One thing softens it: earned cards are saved right away (durum.i.album.push + kaydetDurum, oyun.ts:225-226), so the album itself keeps them. But albumOnce is read again on rebuild (oyun.ts:66, hafizaOyunu.ts:35), so cards earned before the album visit are left out of the end-of-round new-card and unlock count, as claimed. The path is easy to reach, and no guard prevents it.

confirmed.title: Tapping a theme or age card, then Home/Back/Album/Parent within ~1 s, still jumps into the game
confirmed.scenario: On the packs screen the child taps a pack, then changes their mind and taps Home (or Album, or the parent button) while 'X! Başlıyoruz!' is playing. The app goes to the requested screen, then a moment later switches to the game on its own. With the parent button, the game starts under the open parent gate and its question audio cuts off the gate prompt. If the parent then solves the gate, the round just started is thrown away. The age screen has the same problem: tap an age, then Back, and you land on acilis and are then pulled into temalar.
confirmed.evidence: temalar.ts:65-69: `kilit = true; ... await Promise.all([konus(...), bekle(sure(700))]); app.git(hafizaModu ? 'hafiza' : 'oyun', { tema: t.id });`. `kilit` only guards the pack cards and the Hafıza strip. The Home button (line 102: `() => app.git('acilis')`), the album button (line 91) and the parent button (line 93) still work. `app.git` calls `sus()`, which resolves the pending `konus` at once, so after the 700 ms wait the stale handler navigates anyway; there is no 'still on this screen' check. Same pattern in yas.ts:31-32 (`await Promise.all([konus(...), bekle(sure(900))]); app.git(param?.sonra ?? 'temalar', ...)`) while the Back button (yas.ts `() => app.git('acilis')`) stays active.
reasons:
CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug can happen in the shipped app. Both screens are registered in src/oyun.ts:23-24, so a user reaches them normally.

temalar.ts: when a card is tapped, the handler at lines 66-70 sets the local `kilit` and then awaits `Promise.all([konus(...), bekle(sure(700))])`. After that it calls `app.git(...)` without checking that this screen is still the active one. Only the card handlers (line 58) and the Hafıza strip (line 86) look at `kilit`. The Home button (line 103), Album (line 92) and Parent (lines 93-94) go through `yuvarlakDugme` (ui/ortak.ts:7-13), which only plays `efekt.dokunma()` and runs the callback, so they keep working.

Nothing blocks those taps. `.paket.yeni-acildi` (ana.css:1135) is only an animation plus a box-shadow. The `.ekran.cikiyor` rule (`pointer-events:none`, ana.css:97-101) only applies once a screen is leaving.

`Uygulama.git` (uygulama.ts:72-100) has no screen-generation or "still active" guard. It calls `sus()` (konusma.ts:50-62), which bumps `sayac` and calls `bitir?.()`. That ends the pending `konus` early, and even without it the `konus` promise would settle on its own. So the 700 ms `bekle` is the only thing still pending, and after it the stale closure runs `app.git('oyun'|'hafiza')` on top of whatever screen the user moved to.

With the Parent button, `ebeveynKapisi` is awaited while the stale handler fires. The game screen opens and its `konus` calls `sus()`, which cuts off the gate prompt. When the gate is solved, `app.git('ebeveyn')` replaces the game.

yas.ts:24-32 has the same pattern with `bekle(sure(900))`. The Back button at line 43 (`app.git('acilis')`) is not gated by `kilit`, so the user lands on acilis and is then pulled into `param.sonra ?? 'temalar'`.

The window is about 0.7-0.9 s plus however long the speech takes. A child can easily tap in that time on a phone or on the website.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. The bug happens as described, and nothing in the code shows it is deliberate.

1. **temalar.ts:66-70.** The pack card sets `kilit = true`, then waits for `Promise.all([konus(tema_basla), bekle(sure(700))])` and calls `app.git(...)` without checking whether this screen is still the active one. `kilit` is only checked by the pack cards (line 58) and the Hafıza strip (line 86). The Home button (line 103), the Album button (line 92) and the parent button (lines 93-94) do not check it.

2. **`app.git` has no guard.** In uygulama.ts:72-99 there is no token or "is this screen still active" check. It calls `sus()` and replaces the current screen.

3. **The pending speech resolves at once.** `sus()` (konusma.ts:50-62) calls `kayitDurdur()`, which runs `calanBitti`, so the recorded-audio promise resolves (kayit.ts:128 and 156-158). It also calls `bitir?.()`, which ends the device-voice part. After that the `konus` loop exits because `benim !== sayac`. So `Promise.all` finishes once the 700 ms wait ends, and the old handler navigates to `oyun`/`hafiza` anyway. The child lands on Home or the Album and is then pulled into the game.

If the parent solves the gate, `app.git('ebeveyn')` leaves the round that just started.

6. **Intent.** No comment, note or spec explains this. `kilit` exists only to stop double taps on the cards. Other code does check staleness (for example `eslestir.ts:150 !hedef.isConnected`), so the missing check here is an oversight. Going to a screen the child did not ask for, and starting a round under the parent gate, is wrong behaviour, not something harmless.

7. **Can a child hit it?** The window is the length of the "{tema}! Başlıyoruz!" clip, at least 700 ms. That is easy to hit on a phone.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. Nothing in the code stops the late navigation. In temalar.ts:66-70, `kilit` is checked only by the pack cards (line 58) and the Hafıza strip (line 86). The Home button (line 103), the album button (line 92) and the parent button (line 93) are plain yuvarlakDugme handlers (ortak.ts:9-12) with no lock. It has no navigation token, and the old handler never checks whether it is still the active screen. sus() increments `sayac` and calls `bitir`, so the pending konus() resolves early, or ends at the `benim !== sayac` check. After bekle(sure(700)) the stale closure runs app.git('oyun'/'hafiza', {tema}) on its own. yas.ts:31-32 has the same problem with the Back button on line 43. The window is about 0.7 s up to the length of the "X! Başlıyoruz!" speech. A child who taps a pack and then quickly taps Home or Album lands on the chosen screen and is yanked into the game about a second later. With the parent button, the game screen is built while the gate is open, and the game's question audio cuts off the gate prompt. A parent or a store reviewer tapping around would plausibly notice this.

confirmed.title: 'Yeni paket açıldı!' celebration is lost for good if the child taps Tekrar or leaves before it appears
confirmed.scenario: A round pushes the album past an unlock threshold (6, 14, 22 or 30 cards). The end screen shows 'Tekrar oyna' and 'Yeni tema' right away, but the unlock celebration only appears after the stars and the speech, about 4-5 s. A child who taps 'Tekrar oyna' early never sees 'Yeni paket açıldı!', and it is never shown later either. The same loss happens when the threshold is crossed mid-round and the child leaves with Home or Android Back before finishing. The pack does unlock, but the child never gets the reward moment or hears that a new pack exists.
confirmed.evidence: The celebration loop runs only after `await Promise.all([konusma, bekle(...)]); if (kapandi) return;` (turSonu.ts:66-67). `durum.i.kutlananTemalar.push(id)` (line 70) is reached only if the screen is still open. Unlocks are found only by comparing counts at round start and end: `yeniAcilanlar(albumOnce, i.album.length, ...)` with `albumOnce` taken when the screen is built (oyun.ts:65, 255; hafizaOyunu.ts:35, 189). Once the round where the threshold was crossed is over, no later round detects that pack again, so it is never celebrated. Hafıza Oyunu's bitir loop has the same `if (kapandi ...) continue` before the push.
reasons:
CONFIRM: I could not refute it. Both paths are reachable in the shipped app.

1) Tapping 'Tekrar oyna' early: in turSonu.ts:26 the button is active from the moment the screen is built. It calls app.git('oyun'), and git() runs eski.kapat() (uygulama.ts:77), which sets kapandi=true. The async loop then exits at line 57 or 67, so it never reaches `kutlananTemalar.push` (line 70) or paketKutla. The only trace left is the 'yeni-acildi' highlight on the 'Yeni tema' path (temalar.ts:56), and Tekrar does not pass that either.

2) Leaving mid-round: oyun.ts:225-226 pushes each reward card into durum.i.album and saves it right away (kaydetDurum). Leaving with Home (app.git('temalar')) or Back means bitir() never runs, so yeniAcilanlar is never computed. The next round's albumOnce (oyun.ts:66) already counts past the threshold, so yeniAcilanlar(onceki, sonraki) (odul.ts:53-54) only finds packs whose threshold is crossed during that round. The same applies to hafizaOyunu.ts:35/142-143/189.

Nothing else re-celebrates an unlocked pack that was never celebrated: kutlananTemalar is only read and written in these two loops. The thresholds 6/14/22/30 are real (content/temalar.json).

Impact: the pack still unlocks; only the celebration and the announcement are lost.

confirmed.title: iOS: saving the 'Kartım' card to Photos crashes the app (NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription is missing)
confirmed.scenario: iOS app, after a drawing comes to life, a parent taps the Kartım (share) icon. One of two things happens. (a) WKWebView supports navigator.share with files, so the system share sheet opens and the parent picks 'Save Image'. (b) Without share support, the fallback popup tells the user to long-press the image; the image has -webkit-touch-callout: default, so iOS shows its 'Save to Photos'/'Add to Photos' menu. Both paths write to the photo library. iOS kills any app that touches photo-library writes without the usage-description key. The app crashes, and an App Store reviewer trying this would see the crash.
confirmed.evidence: kart.ts:172-174 calls nav.share({ files: [dosya] ... }). ekranlar.ts:459-462 fallback says 'Resmi basılı tutup kaydedebilirsin.' and canlan.css:1022 sets `-webkit-touch-callout: default` on `.cc-kart-pencere img`. ios/App/App/Info.plist has only NSMicrophoneUsageDescription among privacy keys. NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription is missing.
reasons:
REFUTE: The tap path is real, but I don't believe it leads to a crash. canlan is in the app build: vite.config.ts UYGULAMADA_YOK leaves out only sesTesti, orman, uygulama, gizlilik and sartlar. The Kartım button is shown after the drawing comes to life (ekranlar.ts:677). It calls kartPaylas (ekranlar.ts:525), which uses nav.share({files}) when canShare allows it (kart.ts:172-174) and otherwise opens kartPenceresi (ekranlar.ts:459-462), where canlan.css:1022 turns the long-press menu on.

The crash itself is not supported. The app never calls a photo-library API: there is no Capacitor Camera or Filesystem plugin, and nothing in src/kabuk or canlan touches photos. Both save paths are system UI, and as far as I know the system checks for the key before offering a save option.
(b) WKWebView's long-press image menu (WebKit's WKActionSheetAssistant) only includes the Save/Add to Photos action when the host app's Info.plist declares a photo-library usage description. Without the key the option is simply missing, so the user can't reach a save.
(a) In UIActivityViewController, which is what WebKit's share sheet presents, 'Save Image' (SaveToCameraRoll) is not offered when NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription is missing. That is the well-known 'Save Image missing from the share sheet' symptom. The 'crash on Save Image' reports come from the iOS 11 era, and file sharing through navigator.share in WKWebView only exists on much later iOS versions.

So the realistic result is a smaller UX bug, not a crash or a reviewer rejection: the share sheet has no 'Save Image' and the long-press menu has no save option, which makes the fallback hint 'Resmi basılı tutup kaydedebilirsin.' misleading inside the iOS app. Adding NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription fixes that, but the claimed 'high' crash does not happen.

In the share sheet the obvious choice is 'Save Image', and in WKWebView a long-press gives 'Save to Photos/Add to Photos'. Both are photo-library additions. ios/App/App/Info.plist declares only NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, with no NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription. I found no note or spec saying this was left out on purpose. iOS ends the process with the privacy-usage crash when a photo-library add happens without that key; this is a well-known WKWebView/UIActivityViewController crash. confirmed.title: Second finger or palm on the drawing canvas links the strokes and ends the first stroke
confirmed.scenario: A 3-4 year old draws with one finger while another finger or the palm rests on the paper, which is very common on phones. The second pointerdown replaces `aktif`. From then on both fingers' pointermove events get pushed into the same stroke, so a zig-zag line jumps back and forth between the two touch points. When either finger lifts, birak() clears `aktif` and the other finger stops drawing. In iz mode the zig-zag also lights up path dots wrongly, because geriBildirim reads the last stroke. In nokta mode every stray touch counts as `hata++` (nokta.ts:255), which lowers the stars.
confirmed.evidence: tuval.ts:39-58: bas() always does `this.aktif = {...}; this.cizgiler.push(this.aktif)`. surukle() pushes points from any pointer into `this.aktif` without checking e.pointerId. birak() on any pointerup sets aktif=null. Nothing tracks the active pointer.

CONFIRM: I could not refute the main claim. It is reachable in the shipped app. Tuval is only used by Çiz Canlansın (canlan/src/ekranlar.ts:237), which is a real Vite entry (vite.config.ts:12, 'canlan/index.html'). The canvas sets touchAction='none' (tuval.ts:23). Nothing filters by pointerType or isPrimary, and no handler stores a pointerId. bas() (tuval.ts:39-45) always replaces `aktif` and pushes a new stroke. surukle() (47-52) adds points from any pointer to `aktif`. birak() (54-58) runs on any pointerup, pointercancel or pointerleave and sets aktif=null.

confirmed.title: Leaving an episode while a line is being spoken plays the next line on the menu
confirmed.scenario: In Elektrikler Kesildi! scene 1, Mino says M.kesildi, M.korktu and M.cagir one after another. The child taps Çık during M.kesildi. The menu (açılış) appears, but Mino's next line (M.korktu) plays in full over the menu and its subtitle text is set on the screen that was just removed. The same happens in Salıncak, Banyo and Ege, and also with 'Bir daha': whenever the line cut short is followed directly by another mSoyle/kSoyle/anneSoyle, that next line plays.

That flag is set only inside the rAF loop (elektrik.ts:373 `if (ui.kapandiMi() && !kapandi) kapandi = true`), and the loop has not run yet in the same microtask. So the next `await mSoyle(...)` passes `if (kapandi)` and calls konus() for the new line. Nothing cancels that line afterwards: the iptaller only reject gorev promises. ui.kapandiMi() is already true at that point but is never checked. The same pattern is in salincak.ts:509, banyo.ts:364 and ege.ts:524 (mSoyle/kSoyle/anneSoyle).
reasons: CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug is reachable in the shipped app. The Çık button in bolumEkrani (macera/src/ekranlar.ts) calls app.git('acilis'). Uygulama.git (src/uygulama.ts:71-79) then runs three steps in order. First it calls sus(). sus (src/audio/konusma.ts:50) calls kayitDurdur(), which calls calanBitti(), so kayitCal resolves true; on the speech-synthesis path, bitir() resolves tekParca. Because konus() calls sus() first, the clicked Çık has already done its job and nothing is left to stop the new line. confirmed.title: Salıncak scene 2 (count to 10, ages 5-6) is cut short by the 25 s auto-pass before 10 is reached
confirmed.scenario: A 5-6 year old is told to clap once each time the swing comes back, up to 10. Each count needs a full swing, and one swing takes about 2.1 s. A perfect child therefore needs about 20-21 s from the start of the task. If the child misses about 2 swings (or the mic misses 2 claps), the fixed 25 s timer finishes the task: the badge still shows e.g. 7 or 8, Can jumps up shouting 'Sıra bende!' and the scene moves on. This breaks the 'everyone gets the same number' lesson.
confirmed.evidence: saymaGorevi starts `setTimeout(() => coz(), 25000)` as soon as the task begins (salincak.ts:1146), with hedef = ayar.sayi = 10 for ages 5-6 (salincak-mantik.ts:37). SalinimSayaci counts a clap only after the swing has reached its right end again since the last count. The period is 2π/OMEGA with OMEGA = 3 (salincak-mantik.ts:53), about 2.09 s, so 10 counts need at least 9 periods (about 18.9 s) plus the child's first reaction. Each missed swing adds another 2.1 s, and the timeout is not reset by progress.
reasons: CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug can be hit in the shipped app. sahne2 calls saymaGorevi through sesliGorev (salincak.ts:1113). saymaGorevi starts `if (!TEST_MODU) setTimeout(() => coz(), 25000)` (line 1146). Nothing ever clears or resets that timer when the child makes progress. gorev() (lines 468-490) just resolves on whichever coz call comes first. hedef is ayar.sayi, which is 10 for ages 5-6 (salincak-mantik.ts:37: `k ? 5 : 10`). The swing is new Sarkac() with the default OMEGA = 3, and FIZIK is 1 outside test mode (salincak.ts:151), so one swing takes about 2.1 s. SalinimSayaci.alkis() counts the first clap at once. After that, each count needs the swing to reach its right end again: onUc fires sayac.uc() only when yon === 1. That means 10 counts take the child's reaction time plus 9 swing ends, roughly 17-21 s. The only leniency is kabulMu: after one rejected early clap (yanlis >= 1), the next clap is accepted anyway (line 1153). That helps a child who claps too fast. It does nothing for a swing the child skipped or a clap the mic missed, and each of those costs a full 2.1 s. So two or three missed swings are enough to pass 25 s. The scene then resolves with the badge on 7 or 8, and sahne2 goes on to Can's 'Sıra bende!' jump and the next scene. It gets worse on real phones. The physics step caps dt at 0.1 (line 437), so when the frame rate drops the swing slows down, but setTimeout keeps wall-clock time. Backgrounding the app also pauses requestAnimationFrame while the timer keeps running. The 25 s value is meant as a 'takılırsa' fallback, but with a target of 10 it fires while a cooperative child is still counting.

CONFIRM: The bug is real and it is not intended behaviour. At salincak.ts:1146, saymaGorevi starts a fixed 25 s `setTimeout(() => coz(), 25000)` when the task begins. Progress never clears or restarts it, and calling coz() from it ends the task wherever the count is. For ages 5-6, hedef is 10 (salincak-mantik.ts:37). SalinimSayaci (salincak-mantik.ts:169-186) counts the first clap straight away, because hazir starts true. After that, a clap counts only after a new right-end uc() event, and those come once per period (2π/3 ≈ 2.09 s). So a child clapping once per swing, as the "Alkışla say" prompt asks, needs at least about 18.8 s plus reaction time. That leaves only about 2 swings of slack before the timer fires mid-count. Then sahne2 goes on regardless: Can jumps up, the "Sıra bende!" balloon shows and a star is awarded, while the badge still reads, say, 8.

The only thing that softens this is kabulMu: one early clap is wrong, and the next early clap is accepted. So a child who claps fast, or the tap fallback, can finish sooner. But that is not the play the game asks for.

On intent: the comment says the timer is a stuck guard ("takılırsa kendiliğinden geçer", i.e. auto-pass if stuck). The ORTAK_NOTLAR.md decision (2026-09-25) also says "25 sn ilerleme olmazsa", meaning after 25 s with no progress, and even then it calls for a "parmağınla da olur" hint (you can use your finger too), not an auto-pass. The same line is copy-pasted across ege.ts, elektrik.ts and salincak.ts. Here it cuts off a child who is still progressing, not one who is stuck. That breaks the scene's own lesson in ekip/senaryo/salincak.md, "herkese aynı sayıda sallanış" (everyone gets the same number of swings), and the success condition "Son sayıda Can ayağa fırlar" (Can jumps up on the last number). TEST_MODU switches the timer off, so tests would never catch this. It affects real users only.

CONFIRM: The claim holds and a user would notice it. In salincak.ts:1146, `setTimeout(() => coz(), 25000)` starts as soon as the task begins. Progress never resets it, it is not scaled by sure(), and it is skipped only in TEST_MODU. When it fires, coz() runs the normal success path in sahne2 (lines 1114-1129): the badge stays at the last number, Can and canYakin jump with B.sira_bende ("Sıra bende!"), a star is given and the scene moves on.

For ages 5-6, hedef = ayar.sayi = 10 (salincak-mantik.ts:37). SalinimSayaci (salincak-mantik.ts:169-186) counts the first clap at once, because hazir starts true. Every later count needs a new right-end arrival (onUc yon===1). The period is 2π/3, about 2.1 s, and pompa holds the amplitude near 0.3, so the period barely changes. A perfect child needs about 9 × 2.1 ≈ 19 s plus reaction time, which leaves only about 2 spare swings.

So with 2-3 such slips in 10 counts, which is very likely for a 5-6 year old, the timer cuts the task at 7-8. The fallback is meant for a stuck task ("takılırsa kendiliğinden geçer"), but here it also fires while the child is actively making progress, and the badge visibly stops short of 10. This is not a crash, but it is a noticeable wrong experience in the core counting lesson. Medium severity is fair.

confirmed.title: Sayı Bahçesi stop layout and Mino/Kino position are computed once and break when the phone is rotated
confirmed.scenario: Okula Hazırım is not orientation-locked on phones: src/kabuk/yon.ts YATAY_SAYFALAR does not include 'okul', so the page follows the device. Going the other way (portrait to landscape) gives 4 rows squeezed into a ~300 px tall garden, with stops and labels overlapping vertically. Nothing is fixed until the child leaves and comes back.

Lines 296-305 set ikiliYer.style.left/top in px from ikiliYeri() inside a single setTimeout and add `.ok-olculu` (transform:none). confirmed.title: A half-decorated cookie can lock the day: no topping is accepted and it can't be served to anyone
confirmed.scenario: Day 2 or 3. Customer B (kalp, çilek x2) is waiting. The child makes the cookie in the wrong shape (yıldız), creams it and puts one çilek on it. The cookie targets B because B is the only customer. Then customer C walks in with a yıldız order (muz x2). hedefKalem now scores C higher (shape match +4), so the tabak re-targets to C. Now every topping jar slides off to Kino: muz is rejected because the cookie already has çilek, and çilek is rejected because the limit for C is 0. Tapping the tabak picks C as owner and refuses (muz still missing). Dragging it to B or tapping B also refuses, because B still needs a second çilek. Re-creaming never clears toppings, and new oven batches queue behind the tabak forever. The hint hand keeps pointing at the muz jar, which always slides off. The day can never finish, so the child has to leave and loses the day.
confirmed.evidence: susBas: `const k = hedefKalem(bekleyenSiparisler(), parti); ... const sinir = k ? (k.sus === s ? k.susAdet : 0) : EN_COK_SUS; if (hedefParca.susler.length >= sinir || hedefParca.susler.some((x2) => x2 !== s)) { ...kinoYer_ ... return; }`. kalanIs (l.447-453) returns 'sus' while `parcalar.some(x => x.susler.length < k.susAdet)`. Tabak click (l.1067-1077) and drag (l.1049) both refuse when kalanIs is set. model.ts hedefKalem (l.257-272) re-ranks every call by shape/adet/color among all waiting customers, so the target changes when a new customer becomes hazir. Nothing ever removes susler from a parti, and the tabak can only be emptied by servis().
reasons:
CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it. The trigger is reachable in the shipped build: pasta is a Vite entry and SON_OYNANAN=3, so days 2 and 3 are playable. Walking through the claimed path:

1. **Setup.** On day 2 or 3 two customers can wait at once (GUNLER aralik 9000; a second customer arrives when a slot is free). gunPlani only stops the same shape coming twice in a row, so B=kalp çilek×2 followed by C=yıldız muz×2 is a valid plan (kurabiyeKalemi gives susAdet 1-3 when adet is 1). kalipBas lets the child pick any shape, so a wrong-shape yıldız cookie can be made.

2. **First topping.** While B is the only waiting customer, susBas targets B and the first çilek is accepted.

3. **Re-targeting.** Once C is hazir, model.ts hedefKalem (l.257-272) scores C at 4 (shape) + 2 (adet) and B at no more than 3, so every call now targets C.

4. **Every topping refused.** In susBas (gun.ts l.981):
   - muz: sinir is 2, but `susler.some(x2 => x2 !== s)` is true because the cookie already has çilek, so it is rejected.
   - çilek: k.sus is muz, so sinir is 0 and it is rejected.

5. **Can't serve.** kalanIs (l.447-453) returns 'sus' for both C (1<2) and B (1<2). The tabak click (l.1067-1077, sahibi gives C), the drag (l.1049) and musteriBas (l.463) all refuse.

6. **No way out.**
   - kremaBas only overwrites renk and never clears susler.
   - Nothing in gun.ts empties susler.
   - tabak is cleared only in servis (l.534).
   - Customers never leave: when patience runs out they just fall asleep (sabir dolunca uyu, "gitmez").
   - New oven batches go into `bekleyen` behind the tabak.

7. **Hint hand.** siradakiAdim keeps pointing at the muz jar (k.sus), which always slides off.

The day can't finish. The one condition is that C's susAdet is larger than the topping already on the cookie (2 or more here), and the plan generator allows that.

CONFIRM: I traced the scenario through the code and it really happens. Nothing guards against it, and it is not designed behaviour: the comments say wrong taps should be harmless (gun.ts:693 "yanlış dokunuş zararsız", gun.ts:983 "zararsız").

1. **Any shape can be baked.** kalipBas (gun.ts:730) and firinaKoy (l.748) accept any mould, so a yıldız cookie can be made for a kalp order.
2. **The target follows the best-scoring customer.** hedefKalem (model.ts:257-272) re-scores every waiting customer on each call: shape match is +4, count match +2, colour +1. Once C (yıldız, muz x2) becomes hazir, C outscores B (kalp, çilek x2).
3. **Every topping is refused.** In susBas (gun.ts:976-987), muz is refused because the cookie already has a çilek (`susler.some(x2 => x2 !== s)`). Çilek is refused because `sinir = k.sus === s ? k.susAdet : 0` is 0 for C.
4. **The tabak cannot be served.** Tap: sahibi() picks C, then kalanIs(tabak, C) returns 'sus' because 1 < 2, so it refuses (l.1073). Drag or tap on B: kalanIs(tabak, B) also returns 'sus' because 1 < 2, so it refuses (l.1049 and l.463).
5. **Nothing frees the tabak.** Re-creaming (kremaBas) changes only the colour, worth +1, which cannot outweigh the +4 shape match. No code clears susler, and `tabak` is reassigned only in servis (l.534) and in gozBas when the tabak is empty (l.926). New oven batches just queue in `bekleyen`.
6. **Customers never leave.** When patience runs out they only fall asleep (musteri.ts:307, GUNLER comment "gitmez"), so B and C stay forever.
7. **The day cannot end.** gunBitti runs only when biten >= MUSTERI_TOPLAM (gun.ts:588), and that needs servis.
8. **The hint is a dead end.** siradakiAdim (l.641-648) keeps pointing at C's muz jar, which always slides off.

It is reachable for a real user. On Day 2-3 orders have 1-3 toppings, up to 2 customers can wait at once, a new one arrives at least 9 s after the last, and sabir is 120 s.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. The deadlock is real and a child would hit it.

1. **The setup happens.** On days 2 and 3 every order has a topping (model.ts kurabiyeKalemi l.167-172). The game lets the child bake the wrong shape, since kalipBas (gun.ts l.730-745) accepts any shape. A second customer can arrive while the first is still waiting: up to 2 at once, about 9 s apart.
2. **The target switches.** hedefKalem (model.ts l.257-272) re-scores every waiting customer on each call. A yıldız cookie scores 4+ for a yıldız customer C, against 3 at most for the kalp customer B. So C wins as soon as C becomes hazir.
3. **No topping can be added.** susBas (gun.ts l.976-987) uses that global target. Muz fails because the cookie already has a çilek on it. Çilek fails because its limit is 0 when C wants muz.
4. **The cookie can't be served.** Tapping B or dragging the tabak to B checks only B's order (l.463, l.1049). B still needs a second çilek, so kalanIs (l.451) returns 'sus' and the serve is refused. Tapping the tabak (l.1067-1077) picks C as owner and refuses too, because muz is missing.
5. **Nothing gets the game out of it.**
   - Nothing ever clears susler; kremaBas only sets renk.
   - The tabak can't be thrown away: `tabak =` is only set at l.534 in servis and at l.926.
   - New batches wait in bekleyen behind the tabak.
   - Customers never leave; when patience runs out they only fall asleep (GUNLER comment l.114).
   - The day ends only when every customer is served (l.588).
   - siradakiAdim (l.648) keeps the hint on the muz jar, and tapping it always slides the muz off to Kino.

The day can't be finished, and a parent or reviewer would see the game freeze. It needs C's topping to differ from B's, which is 2 in 3 for a random draw. A wrong cream colour on the cookie, a common slip for 3-6 year olds, can also re-target the cookie the same way.

confirmed.title: Serving a sleeping customer by tapping or dragging the tabak never wakes them: they eat and dance with eyes closed and Zzz showing
confirmed.scenario: A slow child lets a customer's patience heart fill, so the customer falls asleep (ps-uyuyor). The child then taps the ready tabak, which is the main serving path, or drags it onto the customer. The customer gets the cookie, celebrates, eats, dances and walks off with eyes closed, head drooped, the floating 'z z Z' and a dimmed balloon. The 'uyandı' line never plays.
confirmed.evidence: Only musteriBas (l.458-461) calls `m.uyan()`. servis() (l.526-538) checks only `m.bitti || !m.hazir` and never wakes. Tabak click calls `void servis(m)` (l.1078) and drag-drop calls `void servis(m)` (l.1052) directly. musteri.ts poz() keeps `p.gozKapali = true` while `this.uyuyor`, and pasta.css:1112 `.ps-uyuyor .ps-m-zzz { opacity: 1 }` / 1205 `.ps-uyuyor .ps-balon { opacity: .55 }` stay active.
reasons: CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug is reachable in the shipped app: pasta is a real Vite entry in vite.config.ts:17. A customer falls asleep when sabirGuncelle reaches 1 (musteri.ts:307 calls uyu(), which sets uyuyor and adds ps-uyuyor), and stays hazir and !bitti. No serving path skips a sleeping customer. bekleyenSiparisler (gun.ts:439) and musteriAt (gun.ts:1014) filter only on hazir and !bitti, so a tap on the tabak (sahibi() leading to servis(m) at l.1078) and a drag-drop (l.1052) both reach servis() with the sleeping customer. servis() (l.526-588) checks only parti, bitti and hazir. It never calls m.uyan(). The only uyan() call is musteriBas l.459, and grep finds nothing else that clears uyuyor or ps-uyuyor. So all of the following runs while the customer is still asleep: mutlu, ye, dans, git. During that time Karakter.ekHareket (karakter.ts:345, which runs after the animation pose) calls Musteri.poz, and poz keeps setting gozKapali=true and the drooped head (musteri.ts:177-185). The CSS rule `.ps-uyuyor .ps-m-zzz{opacity:1}` (pasta.css:1112) also stays active. The "uyandı" line plays only through musteriBas. One correction: on an exact-match serve the balloon is hidden, not dimmed, because `.ps-kok .ps-bitti:not([data-sonuc='farkli']) .ps-balon{opacity:0}` (l.1208) is more specific than the l.1205 rule. The dimmed balloon appears only on a 'farkli' (different) serve. The closed eyes, Zzz, head droop and missing wake line are all real.

CONFIRM: The bug is real, it is reachable, and nothing shows it was done on purpose. Only musteriBas (gun.ts:458-461) calls m.uyan() and plays P.musteri.uyandi. servis() (gun.ts:526-538) checks only !parti || m.bitti || !m.hazir. Both the tabak click (l.1061-1078, which picks sahibi(tabak) and has no uyuyor check) and the drag-drop (l.1052) call servis(m) directly. Neither those paths nor musteriAt skip a sleeping customer, and nothing in servis, mutlu(), ye() or dans() clears uyuyor or removes the ps-uyuyor class. In musteri.ts, poz() runs as ekHareket after the animation step (karakter.ts:345), so it overrides gozKapali=true, the head droop and the drooping ears during the 'ye' and 'dans' animations. The real e2e test pasta.spec.ts:174 shows the 'mutlu' expression is set for 1600 or 2600 ms (ayni: m.mutlu(2600); farkli: m.mutlu(1600)), but it can only hide the closed eyes for that short window. The Zzz always stays: pasta.css:1112 has no ps-bitti override. On a 'farkli' serve the balloon also stays dimmed (1205); on an 'ayni' serve the higher-specificity rule at 1208 hides it, so that part of the claim only holds for 'farkli'. Intent: ekip/senaryo/pasta-otobusu.md:39 says a sleeping customer "Dokununca uyanır: 'Hı? Sıra bende mi?'". The only test for this, tests/e2e/pasta.spec.ts:174, wakes the customer by clicking the customer itself. No comment or note says a served customer should stay asleep. A child sees a customer eating and dancing with the Zzz still floating over its head and the head drooped, and the wake-up line from the spec never plays. That is wrong, though harmless. The reward is not affected, since m.uyudu was already set. Severity is low to medium, but the claim stands.

CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug happens, and it is easy to see. In pasta/src/gun.ts, `uyan()` is called only from musteriBas (l.458-461). servis() (l.526) checks only `!parti || m.bitti || !m.hazir`. Tapping the tabak (l.1078) and dropping it on a customer (l.1052) both call servis(m) directly. sahibi() picks from bekleyenSiparisler(), which is just `hazir && !bitti` (l.439), so a sleeping customer is a normal serving target. Nothing that runs after that wakes them: m.mutlu(), m.ye(), m.dans() and m.git() (musteri.ts l.361-430, l.291) never touch `uyuyor` or remove `ps-uyuyor`. While `uyuyor` is true, the poz() hook (l.168-185) keeps setting `p.gozKapali = true` with the head drooped and ears down, and the `.ps-uyuyor .ps-m-zzz {opacity:1}` rule (pasta.css:1112) keeps the floating 'z z Z' showing. So during the confetti, the big heart, the three 'ham' bites, the dance and the walk off, the customer stays visibly asleep, and the 'uyandi' line never plays. One part of the claim is overstated: for a correct order the balloon is hidden anyway, because the more specific `.ps-bitti:not([data-sonuc='farkli']) .ps-balon {opacity:0}` (l.1208) wins over the dimming rule. The closed eyes and the Zzz are the visible problem. This is a likely path: a slow 3-4 year old lets the patience heart fill, then taps the ready tabak, which is the main way to serve. A parent or store reviewer would notice a celebration with a sleeping customer as a glitch.

confirmed.title: Evening screen: tapping the piggy bank during the star animation breaks the counting voice and leaves the piggy bank pulsing forever
confirmed.scenario: The evening screen opens with the coin pile and piggy bank on screen right away. The child taps the piggy bank while the stars are still filling, which is very natural. say() starts counting 'Bir!', 'İki!'... The intro coroutine keeps running and calls konus('Üç yıldız!'), which cuts off the number being counted. Then konus('Kumbarada kaç jeton var?') cuts the next number, so the child hears the question in the middle of the count. The intro also adds ps-cagir after say() has already removed it. The piggy bank keeps its infinite 'tap me' pulse through the shop and until the screen closes, and tapping it only jiggles.
confirmed.evidence: The intro IIFE (l.314-323) runs `await yildizGoster(); ... if (kazanc > 0) { kumbara.classList.add('ps-cagir'); await konus(P.mino.kumbara); }` with no `sayildi` check. The kumbara click handler (l.286-289) is live from construction and say() does `kumbara.classList.remove('ps-cagir')` (l.246) at its start. konus() calls sus() first (src/audio/konusma.ts), so each new line cuts the current one. pasta.css:2052 `.ps-kumbara.ps-cagir { animation: ps-ipucu 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; }`.
reasons: CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it. The tap is reachable in the shipped build. pasta/index.html is a Vite entry (vite.config l.17), and gun.ts:1116 opens the evening screen with app.git('aksam', { kazanc: bugun, ... }), so kazanc > 0 after a normal day. In aksamEkrani the coin pile (yigin) and the piggy bank button (button.ps-kumbara) are built and shown at once. The click handler is attached when the screen is built (ekranlar.ts:286-290), and I found nothing that blocks input. Neither .ps-kumbara nor its parents have pointer-events:none, the only overlay (.ps-aksam-gok) has pointer-events:none, and app.git does no input locking. The intro IIFE (l.314-323) takes roughly 300 + 250 + 380·(stars-1) ms plus the spoken star line, which is a window of about 1.5-3 s. It never checks sayildi. Here is what happens if the child taps in that window. (1) say() sets sayildi=true, removes ps-cagir and calls konus('Bir!'). (2) The intro then calls konus(P.mino.yildiz[...]). konus() calls sus() first (konusma.ts:103), which cancels speech and resolves the pending promise, so the number is cut off. The next count step's konus cuts the star line in turn. (3) Next the intro runs kumbara.classList.add('ps-cagir') and konus('Kumbarada kaç jeton var?'), which cuts the number being counted in the middle of the count. ps-cagir is removed only at l.246, and say() returns early once sayildi is true. So the class stays on, and the infinite animation from pasta.css:2052 runs through the shop until the screen closes. It stops only under prefers-reduced-motion (pasta.css:2275). Later taps only jiggle (l.289). Tapping during the spoken star line is an even wider window: say() cuts that line, the intro's await resolves at once, and the question plus ps-cagir follow during the count.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. The bug happens for real users. In pasta/src/ekranlar.ts, the kumbara button is in the DOM from the start (l.152, l.166) and nothing hides it, disables it or turns off its pointer events during the intro. Its click handler (l.286-290) is live right away and calls say() when sayildi is false, which is the case whenever kazanc > 0 (l.186). The intro IIFE (l.314-323) never checks sayildi. After the 300 ms wait it runs yildizGoster(): the stars fill over 250 ms plus 380 ms for each extra star, then konus(P.mino.yildiz[...]) plays. After that it unconditionally adds 'ps-cagir' and calls konus(P.mino.kumbara). A child who taps the piggy bank in the first ~1-3 s starts say(), and say() calls konus('Bir!'...) (l.253). konus() calls sus() first (src/audio/konusma.ts:103), which bumps sayac and resolves the earlier promise. So the intro's star line and the "Kumbarada kaç jeton var?" question cut off the number being counted, and the next number cuts them off in turn: the count and the question interleave. say() removes ps-cagir only once, at l.246. The intro adds it back later at l.320, and nothing removes it after that: not rafAc(), not rafBas, not the tamam handler. pasta.css:2052 gives '.ps-kumbara.ps-cagir' an infinite ps-ipucu animation, so the piggy bank keeps its 'tap me' pulse through the shop, and tapping it only jiggles it (l.289). I found nothing suggesting this is deliberate. The spec (ekip/senaryo/pasta-otobusu.md:56-57, 91) says to tap the piggy bank and then count together, and the question is meant to come before the count. The only e2e test (tests/e2e/pasta.spec.ts:82) runs in TEST_MODU, where konus resolves in 5 ms, so it would not catch this. For a child the result is confusing: the count is cut off and the question comes in the middle of it, and the 'tap me' hint is wrong because tapping does nothing useful. Medium severity is fair.

CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it; the code confirms the claim. In aksamEkrani (pasta/src/ekranlar.ts) the kumbara button exists from the start. It is not disabled and has no visibility or pointer guard, and its click handler (l.286-290) calls say() whenever `sayildi` is false. That is the case for the whole intro whenever kazanc > 0 (l.186). Nothing in the intro IIFE (l.314-323) checks `sayildi`. After yildizGoster() it still calls konus(P.mino.yildiz[...]) ('Üç yıldız!', l.183), then adds 'ps-cagir' and calls konus('Kumbarada kaç jeton var?') (l.320-321). konus() always calls sus() first (src/audio/konusma.ts:102-103). sus() bumps `sayac`, cancels speech or recordings and resolves the current line early. So each line cuts off whatever is playing. For kazanc ≤ 10, sayim() gives one spoken word per coin ('Bir!', 'İki!'...). The star line and the question therefore land in the middle of the count and cut numbers short, and the next number then cuts the question. The tap window is 300ms + 250ms + 380ms per extra star, plus the star line itself, so roughly 1.5-3 s. The piggy bank is the biggest tappable thing on screen, so a child tapping early is very plausible. say() removes ps-cagir only once, at its start (l.246), and nothing removes it later. So the intro's later add leaves the infinite `animation: ps-ipucu 1.2s infinite` (pasta.css:2052) running through the shop until the screen closes. Only the reduced-motion rule at pasta.css:2275 turns it off. Impact: in a counting lesson, a parent or child would hear the numbers chopped and the question asked mid-count. The bank also keeps pulsing 'tap me' after its job is done, and tapping it only jiggles. That is a visible, audible flaw, not a test-only path.

confirmed.title: The day's coins are lost if the evening screen is left before the piggy-bank count finishes
confirmed.scenario: The child finishes a day (earns, say, 14 coins). The evening screen marks the day done (stars, next day unlocked) right away, but the coins only go into the kumbara when the child taps it and the count completes. If the parent presses the Android back button on the evening screen (Pasta has no back handler, so this goes to the main menu), or the app is closed before the count finishes, the coins are gone. The next visit shows the old kumbara total and the shop items stay unaffordable. Replaying the day is the only fix.
confirmed.evidence: `gunBitti(gun, yildiz)` is saved at construction (l.141), but `kazanc` is only added inside say(): `kayit.jeton += adim[i]` (l.263) and `kaydet()` (l.270) after the loop. say() runs only from the kumbara click (l.286-288). No kaydet happens for kazanc anywhere else. The pasta code does not listen for GERI_OLAYI (src/kabuk/yerel.ts backButton → 'menu' → location.assign).
reasons: CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it. The bug can happen in the shipped app. Pasta is a shipped page: it is in vite.config.ts as `pasta: 'pasta/index.html'` and in src/engine/erisim.ts as `pasta: 'abonelik'`. When a day ends, gun.ts:1116 calls `app.git('aksam', { gun, kazanc: bugun, ... })`. In gun.ts, `bugun` only counts coins locally and never touches `kayit.jeton`. aksamEkrani then saves the day right away with `gunBitti(gun, yildiz)` (ekranlar.ts:141). The only places that add `kazanc` to the kumbara are `kayit.jeton += adim[i]` (l.263) and `kaydet()` (l.270) inside say(). say() runs only from the kumbara click handler (l.286-288). A search over pasta/src finds no other write to `kayit.jeton` except the `?jeton=` test shortcut in oyun.ts:32. The only exit inside the evening screen is the Tamam button, which stays hidden until rafAc(); when kazanc>0, rafAc() only runs at the end of say(). The evening screen's top bar has no back button, only a 56px spacer. Exits outside the game are still open, though. pasta/src/main.ts and oyun.ts never call geriDinle, so on Android the back button sends GERI_OLAYI and nothing cancels it. geriKarari then returns 'menu', and yerel.ts:173-177 runs `location.assign(menu)`. The page unloads with no kaydet. If the child is partway through the count, the in-memory jeton additions are lost too, because kaydet only runs after the loop. Closing the app or the browser tab before tapping the kumbara has the same effect. The day stays marked done but its coins are never saved. The trigger is easy to hit: the child just has to leave or press back instead of tapping the glowing kumbara.

CONFIRM: I could not refute this. In pasta/src/ekranlar.ts, aksamEkrani saves the day as finished as soon as the screen is built (gunBitti(gun, yildiz) at l.141). The day's coins are only added inside say(): `kayit.jeton += adim[i]` at l.263, then kaydet() at l.270. say() runs only when the child taps the kumbara (l.286-288). Nothing else in pasta/src adds kazanc to kayit.jeton. gun.ts:1116 only passes `kazanc: bugun` to the evening screen, and kapat() (l.327-331) only sets kapandi, with no save.

There is no guard that stops the child leaving early:
- The evening top bar has no exit button (an empty 56px div at l.165), but the Android back button still works. Nothing in pasta listens for GERI_OLAYI or calls geriDinle, so src/kabuk/yerel.ts:166-177 takes the 'menu' route and does location.assign(menu). The page unloads without saving the coins.
- Android killing the app in the background has the same effect.

On intent, I found nothing that makes the loss deliberate. The spec (ekip/senaryo/pasta-otobusu.md l.35/57) says only that the coins fly into the kumbara and Mino counts them. ORTAK_NOTLAR l.318 says nothing about leaving early. The counting animation is there to teach counting; there is no rule that uncounted coins are thrown away.

One partial-safety detail: if kapat() runs in the middle of the count, the loop stops and kaydet() still runs, so only the coins not yet counted are lost. If the child leaves before tapping at all, they lose all of them.

The harm is real but small. The coins only buy cosmetic shelf items, and replaying the day earns them again. But the child sees stars and the next day unlocked, while the coins they just earned never show up in the kumbara total. Medium or low severity seems fair, but the bug is real.

CONFIRM: I couldn't refute it; the code matches the claim. In pasta/src/ekranlar.ts, `aksamEkrani` calls `gunBitti(gun, yildiz)` at l.141. That saves stars and unlocks the next day straight away. The day's `kazanc` reaches `kayit.jeton` only inside `say()` (l.263), and `kaydet()` runs only after the loop (l.270). `say()` is called only from the kumbara click handler (l.286-288). The day's running count `bugun` in gun.ts (l.505) is never written to `kayit` either; it is only passed as a parameter (gun.ts l.1116). `kapat()` (l.327-331) only sets `kapandi` and does not save anything. Neither pasta/src nor src/uygulama listens for GERI_OLAYI, so Android back on the evening screen reaches `geriKarari` → 'menu' → `location.assign` (src/kabuk/yerel.ts l.166-177) and the page unloads. The same happens if the app is closed or killed. If this happens mid-count, the awaits never resume, so the coins added in memory are lost too.

Impact: the evening screen has no in-app exit before the count. Its top bar has only a spacer and the sound button, and the Tamam button stays hidden until `rafAc()`, which needs the count to finish when kazanc>0. So the bug needs back, home-then-kill, or closing the app. A parent closing the app once the day is "finished" is a realistic case, because the stars show first and the kumbara only pulses afterwards. A child who just watched 14 coins go into the kasa will come back to the old kumbara total with shop items still out of reach. The day is already marked done (stars and next day saved), so nothing hints that the coins were never banked. The only fix is replaying a day. That is a visible, if modest, loss of progress, so medium severity is fair.

confirmed.scenario: In any Sesli Macera, Mino says a line that is followed straight away by another one, e.g. dogumgunu.ts:172-173 `await soyle(D.arkadaslar); await soyle(D.surpriz_plan);`. Its konus() calls sus() again (sayac++), which cancels the replay that has just started.
reasons: CONFIRM: I traced the path and the bug is real for users. Nothing guards it. The speaker button is built with yuvarlakDugme (src/ui/ortak.ts:7-12), a plain click handler that calls tekrarDinle with no konusuyorMu or narration check. The balloon is always shown in the chapter's top bar (ekranlar.ts:197,208; no CSS hides it). The el pointerdown handler skips buttons (ekranlar.ts:248-251). tekrarDinle runs `void konus(...)`, and konus calls sus() first (konusma.ts:103). sus does sayac++ and kayitDurdur(), which calls calanBitti, so the in-flight kayitCal resolves (kayit.ts:128,156-158). For device TTS it calls bitir(), which resolves tekParca (konusma.ts:60,147). The old konus loop then sees benim !== sayac and returns (konusma.ts:120/126), so the old promise resolves. dogumgunu.ts soyle (lines 98-102) only does `await konus(t,{ton:1.12})`, so the next `await soyle(D.surpriz_plan)` (line 173) runs on the next microtask. Its konus calls sus() again and bumps sayac. At that point the replay is usually still inside `await tampon(...)` (kayit.ts:117); when that returns, iptalMi() is true and it never plays. If it had started, kayitDurdur stops it. The same pattern holds for mSoyle/kSoyle in banyo, ege, elektrik and salincak. ekranlar.ts and dogumgunu.ts both import konus through src/audio/ses.ts, which re-exports the konusma.ts version, so this is the shipped code path in both the app and the website. The one exception is TEST_MODU. The result: the line the child asked to hear again is cut off and the story jumps to the next line.

CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug is real, reachable, and nothing in the code, notes or tests says it is intended. ekranlar.ts:196 `tekrarDinle = () => void konus(sonYazi, ...)`. konus() calls sus() first (konusma.ts:103), which does sayac++ and then kayitDurdur(). kayitDurdur (kayit.ts:156-158) calls calanBitti, which resolves the in-flight kayitCal as true. The replay's loop checks `benim !== sayac` after `await tampon` (kayit.ts:118) or in the 60 ms speak timeout (konusma.ts:184), so it is cancelled before or right after it starts. The line the child asked for is lost and the story jumps to line B. Nothing stops the tap: yuvarlakDugme (src/ui/ortak.ts:7-13) has no 'currently speaking' guard, and no CSS hides the button while Mino talks. The only comment (ekranlar.ts:194) is about which voice to use. ORTAK_NOTLAR line 265 only mentions the Kino voice for 'Tekrar dinle'. No test covers it. This is wrong behaviour, not deliberate. CONFIRM: I could not refute it. The bug happens as described, and a child would notice it. Code path: `tekrarDinle` (macera/src/ekranlar.ts:196) is `void konus(sonYazi, ...)`, and nothing stops the button from working while a line is playing. There is no konusuyorMu check and no disabled state; the CSS for .mc-altyazi only covers font size and animation. konus() calls sus() first (konusma.ts:103). sus() does sayac++, then kayitDurdur(), which immediately calls calanBitti and resolves the playing kayitCal promise with true (kayit.ts:156-158). For device TTS it calls bitir?.(), which resolves tekParca (konusma.ts:60). The next `await soyle(D.surpriz_plan)` (dogumgunu.ts:172-173) calls ui.yazi(B), so the subtitle switches to the next line. Its konus() calls sus() again, which fades out and stops the replay started a moment before (kayitDurdur ramps to 0 in 0.18 s).
